title: Death, Resurrection and Judgment
summary: What happens when we die, what the Bible teaches about the resurrection of the body, and how God will judge all people.
description: Death is certain, but it is not the end. This course studies what the Bible teaches about death, the state of believers and unbelievers between death and resurrection, views such as soul sleep and purgatory, the bodily resurrection of all people, the judgment seat of Christ and the great white throne, and how these truths should shape Christian living, grieving and funeral practice in an African context.
objectives: Explain the biblical view of death
Describe the intermediate state and evaluate other views
Teach the bodily resurrection of believers and unbelievers
Explain the final judgment and the judgment seat of Christ
Apply these truths to grief, funerals and daily living
outcomes: Explain why death entered the world and how Christ defeated it
Describe what happens to believers and unbelievers at death
Explain the nature of the resurrection body
Distinguish the judgment of believers' works from the final judgment
Evaluate funeral and ancestral practices in the light of Scripture

modules.title: The Last Enemy
modules.intro: Death is an enemy, but a defeated one. This week we study what death is and how Christ has conquered it.

lessons.title: Why we die
lessons.body:
Death was not part of God's original creation. God warned Adam, "in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die" (Genesis 2:17). After the fall, "dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return" (3:19).

"Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned" (Romans 5:12). "The wages of sin is death" (6:23).

Scripture speaks of death as separation: physical death separates soul from body (Ecclesiastes 12:7; James 2:26); spiritual death separates people from God (Ephesians 2:1); and the "second death" is final separation (Revelation 20:14).

lessons.title: Christ has conquered death
lessons.body:
Christ took on flesh "that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil; And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage" (Hebrews 2:14-15).

He rose from the dead, and said, "I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore... and have the keys of hell and of death" (Revelation 1:18).

So Paul can taunt death: "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory? The sting of death is sin... But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 15:55-57). "The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death" (15:26).

lessons.title: Facing death as a Christian
lessons.body:
Because of Christ, believers need not fear death. Paul said, "For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain" (Philippians 1:21). He had "a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better" (1:23).

"Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints" (Psalm 116:15). David said, "though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me" (Psalm 23:4).

This does not mean death is good in itself. Jesus wept at Lazarus' tomb (John 11:35). We may grieve honestly, but "not... as others which have no hope" (1 Thessalonians 4:13).

terms.def: The separation of soul from body.
Separation from God because of sin.
Final, eternal separation from God in the lake of fire (Revelation 20:14).
Death, which Christ will finally destroy (1 Corinthians 15:26).
Sin, which gives death its power to harm (1 Corinthians 15:56).
Christ's authority over death and the grave (Revelation 1:18).

texts.teaches: Death entered the world by sin and passed upon all men.
Christ delivers those who were in bondage through fear of death.
O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
To live is Christ, and to die is gain.
I am the resurrection and the life.

summary: Death entered through sin and comes to all.
Death is separation: physical, spiritual and the second death.
Christ has defeated death and holds its keys.
Believers face death with hope, though they may grieve.

options: Final separation from God in the lake of fire

questions.q: What is the sting of death?
Who holds the keys of hell and of death?
What did Paul say about dying?

modules.title: Between Death and Resurrection
modules.intro: What happens to people immediately after death? This week we study the intermediate state and evaluate other views.

lessons.title: With Christ
lessons.body:
When believers die, their souls go immediately into the presence of Christ. Jesus told the dying thief, "To day shalt thou be with me in paradise" (Luke 23:43). Paul said that to be "absent from the body" is to be "present with the Lord" (2 Corinthians 5:8).

The souls of martyrs are pictured in heaven, conscious and crying out (Revelation 6:9-10). Stephen prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" (Acts 7:59).

This is called the **intermediate state**: a real but incomplete blessedness. Believers are with Christ but still await the resurrection of their bodies.

lessons.title: The rich man and Lazarus
lessons.body:
Jesus told of a rich man and a beggar named Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31). When they died, Lazarus was carried "into Abraham's bosom", while the rich man was "in hell" (Hades) "being in torments" (16:22-23).

The story shows:

- Conscious existence after death.
- An immediate and fixed division: "between us and you there is a great gulf fixed" (16:26).
- No second chance after death (Hebrews 9:27).
- The sufficiency of Scripture: "They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them" (16:29).

The dead do not return to warn or trouble the living.

lessons.title: Soul sleep, purgatory and the ancestors
lessons.body:
**Soul sleep**: Seventh-day Adventists and some others teach that the dead are unconscious until the resurrection, as Scripture often calls death 'sleep' (1 Thessalonians 4:13). Most Christians reply that 'sleep' describes the body's appearance and the temporary nature of death, while the soul is conscious with Christ (Philippians 1:23).

**Purgatory**: the Roman Catholic Church teaches a place of final purification for those who die in God's grace but are not yet fully cleansed. Protestants reply that Christ's blood "cleanseth us from all sin" (1 John 1:7) and that believers go straight to be with the Lord.

**Ancestors**: many African traditions hold that the dead become ancestors who influence the living and must be honoured with sacrifices. Scripture forbids consulting the dead (Deuteronomy 18:10-12; Isaiah 8:19) and points us to Christ as the only Mediator (1 Timothy 2:5).

terms.def: The condition of people between death and the resurrection.
The blessed presence of God where believers go at death.
The realm of the dead; in Luke 16, a place of torment for the unrighteous.
The view that the dead are unconscious until the resurrection.
In Catholic teaching, a state of final purification after death.
Attempting to consult or communicate with the dead, forbidden in Scripture.

texts.teaches: Today you shall be with me in paradise.
Absent from the body is present with the Lord.
A great gulf is fixed between the saved and the lost after death.
It is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.
God forbids consulting with familiar spirits and the dead.

summary: Believers go immediately to be with Christ at death.
Luke 16 shows conscious existence and a fixed division after death.
There is no second chance after death.
Scripture rejects consulting the dead; Christ is the only Mediator.

questions.q: Where did Jesus tell the thief he would be that day?
What separated the rich man and Lazarus?
What does Hebrews 9:27 say comes after death?

modules.title: The Resurrection of the Body
modules.intro: Christian hope is not escape from the body but resurrection of the body. This week we study what the Bible promises.

lessons.title: All will rise
lessons.body:
Jesus said, "the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation" (John 5:28-29).

Daniel foresaw it: "many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt" (Daniel 12:2). Paul believed "there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust" (Acts 24:15).

The resurrection is bodily. The body that is buried is the body that is raised, though transformed.

lessons.title: The resurrection body
lessons.body:
"But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?" (1 Corinthians 15:35). Paul uses the picture of a seed: what is sown is different from the plant that grows, yet connected to it (15:36-38).

The resurrection body of believers will be:

- **Incorruptible**: never decaying or dying (15:42).
- **Glorious**: no longer weak or dishonoured (15:43).
- **Powerful** (15:43).
- **Spiritual**: fully governed by the Spirit, yet still a real body (15:44).

It will be like Christ's risen body, which could be touched and could eat (Luke 24:39-43; Philippians 3:21).

lessons.title: When the dead in Christ rise
lessons.body:
The resurrection of believers takes place at Christ's return: "For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout... and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them" (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17).

"We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump" (1 Corinthians 15:51-52).

This gives value to the body now. Because God will raise it, we honour it, care for it, and use it for His glory (1 Corinthians 6:13-14, 19-20).

terms.def: The raising of the dead body to life, transformed and reunited with the soul.
The rising of the righteous to everlasting life (John 5:29).
The rising of the wicked to judgment (John 5:29).
Not subject to decay or death.
A real body fully governed and empowered by the Holy Spirit.
The trumpet sounding at Christ's return when the dead are raised.

texts.teaches: The good rise to life and the evil to damnation.
There shall be a resurrection of both the just and the unjust.
The body is sown in corruption and raised in incorruption.
Christ will change our lowly body to be like His glorious body.
The dead in Christ shall rise first.

summary: All people will be raised, some to life and some to damnation.
The resurrection is bodily, like a seed becoming a plant.
Believers' bodies will be incorruptible, glorious, powerful and spiritual.
The dead in Christ rise at His return.

questions.q: Who will be raised, according to Acts 24:15?
options: Both the just and the unjust

questions.q: What picture does Paul use for the resurrection body?
When do the dead in Christ rise?
What will Christ's return change our bodies to be like?

modules.title: The Judgment to Come
modules.intro: Every person will stand before God. This week we study the final judgment and how it should shape our lives and funerals.

lessons.title: The judgment seat of Christ
lessons.body:
"For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad" (2 Corinthians 5:10).

For believers this is not a judgment of condemnation (Romans 8:1) but an evaluation of their service. Each one's work "shall be made manifest... the fire shall try every man's work". Some will receive a reward; others "shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire" (1 Corinthians 3:13-15).

Scripture speaks of crowns: of life (James 1:12), of righteousness (2 Timothy 4:8) and of glory (1 Peter 5:4).

lessons.title: The great white throne
lessons.body:
John saw "a great white throne, and him that sat on it... And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened... and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works" (Revelation 20:11-12).

"Whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire" (20:15).

God's judgment will be perfectly just. He will judge "the secrets of men by Jesus Christ" (Romans 2:16), and people will be judged according to the light they received (Luke 12:47-48). Only those whose names are in the Lamb's book of life will escape condemnation.

lessons.title: Living, grieving and burying well
lessons.body:
The coming judgment calls us to live soberly, to share the gospel (2 Corinthians 5:11) and to forgive others, leaving vengeance to God (Romans 12:19).

In grief, Christians weep but with hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13-18). Funerals should honour the dead, comfort the living and point to Christ.

Practices to avoid: rituals to appease or consult the dead, accusing others of witchcraft for a death, crushing families with debt for lavish burials, and harmful widowhood rites. Scripture calls us to care for widows and orphans (James 1:27) and to bury with dignity and simplicity.

terms.def: The evaluation of believers' works for reward or loss (2 Corinthians 5:10).
The final judgment of the dead described in Revelation 20:11-15.
God's record of those who belong to Him and are saved.
The reward Paul expected for those who love Christ's appearing.
Being saved while losing reward for worthless works (1 Corinthians 3:15).
Traditional mourning practices for widows, some of which are harmful and unbiblical.

texts.teaches: We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ.
Fire will test every man's work.
The dead were judged according to their works out of the books.
Whoever was not written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.
God will judge the world in righteousness by the man He has ordained.

summary: Believers will appear before Christ's judgment seat for reward or loss.
The great white throne judges the dead according to their works.
Only those in the book of life escape condemnation.
Live soberly, grieve with hope and bury with dignity.

questions.q: What is judged at the judgment seat of Christ?
options: Believers' works for reward or loss

questions.q: What happens to those not written in the book of life?
options: Cast into the lake of fire

questions.q: Which practice should Christians avoid at funerals?

short.q: Name the three kinds of death in Scripture.
short.model: Physical death (soul from body), spiritual death (separation from God) and the second death (final separation in the lake of fire).

short.q: Where do believers go at death? Give two texts.
short.model: Into the presence of Christ (Luke 23:43; 2 Corinthians 5:8).

short.q: What does Luke 16:19-31 teach about life after death?
short.model: People are conscious after death, a fixed gulf divides saved and lost with no second chance, and Scripture is sufficient warning.

short.q: Evaluate the practice of consulting ancestors.
short.model: Scripture forbids consulting the dead (Deuteronomy 18; Isaiah 8:19); Christ is the only Mediator between God and man.

short.q: Describe the resurrection body from 1 Corinthians 15.
short.model: Incorruptible, glorious, powerful and spiritual, like a plant from a seed and like Christ's risen body.

short.q: Distinguish the judgment seat of Christ from the great white throne.
short.model: The judgment seat evaluates believers' works for reward or loss; the great white throne judges the dead, and those not in the book of life are condemned.

lists.q: List four qualities of the resurrection body.
List three views of the state after death that Scripture does not support.
List three crowns promised to believers.

assignments.title: A Christian funeral
assignments.prompt: Describe common funeral and mourning practices in your community. Evaluate them in the light of this course, showing which honour God, which should be changed, and how a Christian family can bury a loved one with hope and dignity.

assignments.title: Comfort for the grieving
assignments.prompt: Write a letter of comfort to a Christian who has lost a believing parent. Use at least five passages from the course on death, the intermediate state and the resurrection.

reading: Anthony A. Hoekema, The Bible and the Future
Byang H. Kato, Theological Pitfalls in Africa
